final.format: 1) Problem + fix carousel: pain on the cover, then 9 inner slides, each one stuck point and the fix that a teacher's eyes, light hands and cues give
final.title: The Part You Cannot See
final.stakes: Stakes: if this does not work, or the viewer does nothing, they keep practising the same backbend alone for more years. They keep guessing what is wrong, and the fear of dropping back stays. Being stuck for a long time is when practice stops being fun and people quit. For AYBKK: the stuck practitioners in Bangkok who would gain most from a Mysore room scroll past, and hands-on help stays misread as forcing.
final.why_care: Why care: you have given years to this practice. Every morning you repeat the same backbend, the same fear, the same guess. What is holding you back may be the part you cannot see, and someone standing at your side could see it.

slides.text: Same backbend for years? It may not be your body. It may be your blind spot.
slides.photo_hint: A backbend (urdhva dhanurasana) seen from the side, with Boonchu next to the student watching or with one light hand at the hips. Pick an older student if there is one (slide 1 rule: a beginner or an elder). Calm body, no strain. Clear wall, window or floor for the big word UNSEEN. The student's face is turned away, seen from behind or not clear, unless that student said yes to this post.

slides.text: The part you cannot see is often the part that is stuck. In a backbend, that is your back and hips. A teacher at your side sees what you cannot.
slides.photo_hint: Side view of a backbend or drop back prep. Boonchu stands at the student's side with his eyes on the back and hips, and his hands light or just ready. The student's face is turned away, seen from behind or not clear, unless that student said yes to this post.
slides.source: none (teacher's own teaching content; Boonchu's 4 Oct Reel line 'We cannot see ourself')

slides.text: What you feel and what you do can be very far apart. You feel your legs are straight. From the side, they are bent. A light hand shows you where straight is.
slides.photo_hint: A forward fold or handstand seen from the side, where Boonchu's light hand guides the legs or hips toward straight. No deep push. The student's face is turned away, seen from behind or not clear, unless that student said yes to this post.
slides.source: none (teacher's own teaching content; his 4 Oct words 'The shape and the feeling... big different' and 'we are still super far away')

slides.text: Copying the shape from a photo can keep you stuck. A photo shows the end, not the steps to get there. A teacher shows you the next small step.
slides.photo_hint: Boonchu helping a student in an early, half-way stage of a twist or backbend, not the full shape (for example the first step into Marichyasana, or the start of a backbend). Keep it different from slide 7's one-spot cue. The student's face is turned away, seen from behind or not clear, unless that student said yes to this post.

slides.text: Good hands-on help is light, much lighter than most people think. It guides and never forces. The teacher checks first, and you can always say no. Your breath leads.
slides.photo_hint: A seated twist (Marichyasana) or a gentle forward fold with ONE light hand on the back or shoulder. Both bodies relaxed. The softest-looking adjustment in the set. The student's face is turned away, seen from behind or not clear, unless that student said yes to this post.
slides.source: none (AYBKK safety rule: the student can say no, the breath leads, light hands, never force, the teacher checks first)

slides.text: Fear of dropping back is smart, not weak. The floor is behind you, out of sight. Hands at your waist give you something to trust. Go when your breath is ready.
slides.photo_hint: A drop back seen from the side, with Boonchu's hands at the student's waist as she goes back or comes up. The student's body looks calm, not scared. The student's face is turned away, seen from behind or not clear, unless that student said yes to this post.

slides.text: You may hold your breath in hard asanas and never know it. The jaw gets tight and the shoulders creep up. One quiet cue, "breathe", and the body often softens.
slides.photo_hint: A backbend, twist or forward fold where low, soft shoulders and a calm body are easy to see, with Boonchu near the student. Do not use a handstand here (in a handstand the shoulders are meant to lift). The student's face is turned away, seen from behind or not clear, unless that student said yes to this post.

slides.text: A cue helps most in the moment you move, not after class. After class, a correction is only words. While you move, your body can feel which part goes which way.
slides.photo_hint: Boonchu caught mid-cue: one hand on one exact spot (hip in a twist, or a shoulder in a backbend), maybe talking, while the student is moving. The student's face is turned away, seen from behind or not clear, unless that student said yes to this post.
slides.source: none (teacher's own teaching content; the method name 'drawing the cortical map' was moved off the slide)

slides.text: A stuck backbend is often a legs problem, not a back problem. Strong legs let the spine lift. A teacher's hand at your thigh shows you where to press.
slides.photo_hint: An experienced practitioner in a deep backbend or advanced asana, seen from the side, getting a light adjustment. Use a photo of his wife only, with her OK. If there is none, use a photo where the main student is clearly not her (for example a male student), so nobody reads that student as his wife. Max 2 photos of one person, never two in a row. The student's face is turned away, seen from behind or not clear, unless that student said yes to this post.
slides.source: none (Plato edit 6 Nov: wife/gymnast story kept only in carousel 2; teaching view, Boonchu to confirm)

slides.text: The habit is the fix, not one adjustment. Same practice, same time, and a teacher who notices when you are gone. In your first 12 weeks, we check your progress.
slides.photo_hint: A wider shot of the morning Mysore room: many mats, everyone doing their own practice, and Boonchu helping one student. It should feel like a daily rhythm. No altar and no Sharath or Guruji photo anywhere in the frame, background included (crop below the window shelves). Only teachers' faces clear; students seen from behind, far away or face turned away, unless they said yes to this post.
slides.source: AYBKK promise and 12-week check from the allowed facts; timing checked in public/bkk.html (hab1d): 'Checked at week 0, 6 and 12.' No results claimed.

final.caption:
Same backbend for years? It may not be your body. It may be your blind spot.
You cannot see your own back. A teacher at your side can.
An adjustment is light help from a teacher's hands. The teacher checks first, your breath leads, and you can always say no.
We have taught Ashtanga in Bangkok for 14 years. Here are 9 stuck points we see, and the fix for each.
Comment aybkk and I'll send you the link.
#aybkk #ashtanga #ashtangabangkok #boonchutanti #mysorestyle
final.notes:
BOONCHU MUST CONFIRM:
1) STUDENT FACES (gate, not a reminder): every photo hint now says the student's face is turned away, seen from behind or not clear, unless that student said yes to this post. Plato's notebook says consent is still not confirmed, and the student app promises 'Only you can see this photo'. Tell me which students in the picks said yes, if any. A separate safety point: use only adjustments that look light and calm, never a deep push (Carne flagged comment threads about force and consent).
2) SLIDE 8, YOUR VIEW AND YOUR WIFE'S STORY: confirm 'Even very skilled people need a teacher's hands now and then. Ballet dancers and gymnasts still have coaches.' is your view (4 Oct). Confirm your wife is OK with the story being told again (it was public in the 4 Oct Reel). The slide is now in your voice ('My wife... asked me'), like the caption's 'I'll send you the link'. Photo: her only, with her OK, or a main student who is clearly not her (for example a man). If neither works, cut sentence 3 (the slide still works at 18 words).
3) METHOD NAME: 'drawing the cortical map' is off slide 7, because 'cortical' fails 10-year-old English and reads like a brain-science claim. Neither name ('drawing the cortical map', 'function over shape') is on the slides or in the caption now. If you pick 'drawing the cortical map' as the name for the year, an optional caption line is 'I call this drawing the cortical map.' (your exact words). I did not use the reader's 'drawing your body's map', because it changes your words.
4) SLIDE 9, 12-WEEK CHECK: the check runs at week 0, 6 and 12 of the first 12 weeks (public/bkk.html hab1d). It does not repeat every 12 weeks. The slide now says 'In your first 12 weeks, we check your progress.' Confirm this is done with each new student. No results are claimed.
5) CAPTION YEAR: the allowed facts say 14 years, but public/bkk.html says 'In 2013 he opened AYBKK in his hometown, Bangkok' (13 years). The caption now says 'since 2013', which matches the site. If you taught in Bangkok before 2013, tell me, and '14 years' can come back.
6) COVER WORD: STUCK became UNSEEN, because STUCK is the Lane A keyword (board.md: Lane A word STUCK, keyword test 26 Oct to 22 Nov) and this is a Lane B post ('Comment aybkk'). If you want STUCK, the post has to become Lane A with the approved STUCK caption. The cover's second line now points at the answer: 'It may be your blind spot.'
7) TEACHING PICTURES (your own teaching, check they match how you teach): slide 1 'back and hips' in a backbend; slide 2 'legs feel straight but from the side they are bent'; slide 3 'a photo shows the end, not the steps; a teacher shows you the next small step'; slide 4 'help is much lighter than most people think, guides and never forces'; slide 5 'fear of dropping back is smart, not weak', hands at the waist; slide 6 breath held in hard asanas, jaw gets tight, shoulders creep up, the 'breathe' cue; slide 7 'a cue helps most in the moment you move; after class a correction is only words'.
8) COVER PHOTO: the 1 Oct rule says slide 1 shows a beginner or an elder. Pick an older student in the backbend if there is one. If not, tell me whether the rule applies to this set, which is for experienced practitioners.
OTHER CHANGES AND CHECKS:
9) Slide 6 photo: no handstand (in a handstand the shoulders lift on purpose). Slide 3 photo: a half-way stage, so it does not repeat slide 7's one-spot cue. Slide 9 photo: no altar and no Sharath or Guruji photo, background included (9 Oct order).
10) Photo picks: Bangkok shala only. Max 2 photos of one person, never two in a row. Mix early and late class times. The cover needs a clear wall or floor for UNSEEN. No awkward or revealing angles, so use side views for backbends.
11) Lane B ask ('Comment aybkk'), Instagram only, under the keyword test until 22 Nov. There is no website, price or 'come practice' on the slides or in the caption. I took the emoji out of the caption hook.
12) No outside studies, quotes or injury numbers. The only date or number in public is 'since 2013' (public/bkk.html) and '12 weeks' (allowed fact). Every inner credit is a series label.
13) Fixes I rejected: making the post Lane A to keep STUCK, and the reader's 'We call it drawing your body's map' (it changes your method words). Every slide is between 16 and 32 words (the cover is 16; slides 1 to 9 are 29 to 32).

issues.problem: 'Every 12 weeks, we check your progress' does not match the real check. The 12-week proof check happens at week 0, 6 and 12 of the student's first 12 weeks (bots/direction.md lines 108 and 113, bkk-api.js bkk_checks, bkk.html hab1d 'Checked at week 0, 6 and 12'). It is not a check that repeats every 12 weeks, so the slide overstates the promise.
issues.fix: Change sentence 3 to 'In your first 12 weeks, we check your progress.' (30 words in total). Notes item 4 can then point to the week 0, 6 and 12 check.

issues.problem: Several photo hints ask for students' faces to be seen ('Calm faces', 'Both relaxed', 'The student looks calm', 'A face that looks soft'), but student photo consent is still not confirmed. Plato's notebook says: consent not confirmed, the student app promises 'Only you can see this photo', and until Boonchu says yes only teacher faces should be clear. Notes 1 only says 'confirm', so it is not a gate. It also mixes photo consent with the safety question of whether the hands look light.
issues.fix: Add one line to every photo hint and to notes 1: 'The student's face is turned away, seen from behind or not clear, unless that student said yes to this post.' Keep 'calm' as a description of the body, not the face.

issues.problem: The text says 'Boonchu's wife is not a beginner, and she still asked him for an adjustment', but the photo hint allows any experienced student ('It could be his wife'). Over a photo of a different woman, viewers will think that student is his wife. That misleads them and exposes the student.
issues.fix: Photo hint: use a photo of his wife only, with her OK. If there is none, use a photo where the main student is clearly not her (for example a male student), or remove sentence 3. The slide still works with 18 words: 'Even very skilled people need a teacher's hands now and then. Gymnasts and ballet dancers still have coaches.'

issues.problem: 'It guides and never pushes' is an absolute claim that the photos can disprove. Twist and forward-fold adjustments, and catching a drop back, use real pressure or support. Experienced viewers who look at slides 5 and 6 can call it untrue, and Carne already flagged force and consent comment threads. The safety rule's own wording is 'never force'.
issues.fix: Change to 'It guides and never forces.' The word count stays at 29.

issues.problem: STUCK is the frozen Lane A keyword in the keyword test (26 Oct to 22 Nov: 'Comment STUCK' for the 180K lane). This post is Lane B ('Comment aybkk'). A huge STUCK on the cover of a Lane B post puts both lanes' words on one post. That breaks 'one ask, one word' and the rule that every carousel uses its own lane's word, and viewers who know the STUCK reels may comment STUCK.
issues.fix: Swap the cover's big word for one that is not a test keyword, for example UNSEEN or YEARS, and keep the two lines. If Boonchu wants to keep STUCK, make the post Lane A instead: use the approved STUCK caption and drop 'Comment aybkk'.

issues.problem: A wide shot of the Mysore room often shows the altar in the background. The standing order (9 Oct) is no photos of Sharath or Guruji in carousels, and the altar is called out because it shows in many room shots.
issues.fix: Add to the slide 9 photo hint: 'No altar and no Sharath or Guruji photo anywhere in the frame, background included.'

issues.problem: Standing order (1 Oct): slide 1 of a carousel should show a beginner or an elder. The cover hint asks for any student in urdhva dhanurasana.
issues.fix: Pick an older student in the backbend for the cover if there is one. If not, ask Boonchu once whether the rule applies to this practitioner-focused set.

issues.problem: STUCK and 'Same backbend for years?' name a real pain the reader feels, so the format holds. The second line, 'Your body may not be the problem', hedges with 'may' and gives the reader no idea where the carousel is going. It flips the belief but never hints at the answer (seeing), so the cover is only half clear in one second. The tension is weak, so the swipe is weak.
issues.fix: Big word STUCK. Text: 'Same backbend for years? It may not be your body. It may be your blind spot.' Credit: '9 notes · swipe'. 'Blind spot' is a 10-year-old word (car mirrors) and points straight at the theme. It also leaves slide 1 ('The part you cannot see...') to explain it, so the two slides do not repeat each other.

issues.problem: Sentence 3, 'A cue tells you which part moves, and which way', repeats slide 7's 'Which part, which way, what for' almost word for word. The photo hint ('one hand on one exact spot') is also the same as slide 7's. It brings in 'cue' before the reader has been shown what a cue is, and 'stuck for years' repeats the cover. 'The work inside it' is abstract.
issues.fix: SHAPE: 'Copying the shape from a photo can keep you stuck. A photo shows the end, not the steps to get there. A teacher shows you the next small step.' (29 words). Photo hint: Boonchu helping a student into an early, half-way stage of a twist or backbend, not the full shape. That keeps it different from slide 7.

issues.problem: The text is good, but the photo hint does not fit it. In a handstand the shoulders are meant to lift toward the ears, so 'the shoulders climb' over a handstand photo reads as a correct handstand, not a tense one. 'The jaw locks' also sounds close to a medical word.
issues.fix: Keep BREATH and sentence 1. Change sentence 2 to: 'The jaw gets tight and the shoulders creep up.' (30 words in total). Photo hint: a backbend, twist or forward fold where a soft face and low shoulders are easy to see, with Boonchu near the student. Do not use a handstand here.

issues.problem: This is the weakest slide. 'Cortical' fails 10-year-old English and sounds like a brain-science claim with no source. Sentence 2 is a fragment that repeats slide 3. No sentence gives the WHY behind 'helps most in the moment you move', so the 'says who?' stays unanswered. There is also no stuck point, so it breaks the problem + fix pattern.
issues.fix: MOMENT: 'A cue helps most in the moment you move, not after class. After class, a correction is only words. While you move, your body can feel which part goes which way.' (31 words). If Boonchu confirms 'drawing the cortical map' as the method name for the year, put it in the caption, not on the slide. A slide version could end 'We call it drawing your body's map.'

issues.problem: 'Boonchu's wife' is written in the third person by a stranger. A new viewer does not know who Boonchu is, and the voice clashes with the caption's first person ('I'll send you the link') and with the 'we' on slides 7 and 9. Otherwise the slide is strong: it breaks the belief that only beginners get adjusted.
issues.fix: SKILLED: 'Even very skilled people need a teacher's hands now and then. Ballet dancers and gymnasts still have coaches. My wife is not a beginner, and she still asked me for an adjustment.' (31 words). Her OK is still needed for the story and for any photo of her (notes item 2).

issues.problem: 'After 14 years of teaching Ashtanga in Bangkok' is a number nobody has checked. The site says AYBKK has run Mysore style since 2013 (public/bkk.html, public/start.html), which makes 13 years, not 14. Notes item 6 also says no numbers are used, but this one is. That breaks the rule never to use a figure in public before it is checked.
issues.fix: Use 'Since 2013, teaching Ashtanga in Bangkok, here are 9 stuck points we see, and the fix for each.' Or have Boonchu confirm the year he started teaching before '14' stays.
